content:
According to Bloomberg, Apple is less than two weeks away from launching a brand-new smart display. The report also added some details about the design of Apple's much-anticipated smart home hub.

Bloomberg reported that this home hub will feature a 6-inch square display. The overall design is reminiscent of the classic iMac G4, which had a hemispherical base with a metal arm supporting the display.

Mark Gurman said the device is "about as thick as an iPhone," with quarter-inch wide black bezels similar to older iPads. The body features rounded corners with "absolutely no sharp edges."

Here are more design details mentioned in the report:

  • The body features Apple's "standard gray aluminum finish," with "rubber on the bottom so it doesn't slip and sits nicely on a table."
  • It has a USB-C port for power, with no built-in battery, so it must be plugged in at all times.
  • The bottom of the device is a "circular metal base with multiple rows of speaker holes."
  • The display is connected to the base by a "polished metal arm."
  • Users can tilt the display forward or backward.
  • There are no volume or power buttons on the device.
  • There is a front-facing FaceTime camera, and no rear camera.

Bloomberg also mentioned that there will be a second version of this home hub, "designed for wall mounting." This version is also powered by USB-C, with a "thin, square base below the display that houses speakers and a microphone." The base is reportedly "mounted flat against the wall, below the screen."

For the full report, head over to Bloomberg. What are your thoughts on Apple's home hub product? Planning to buy one or several? Feel free to share your opinions in the comments section.
